newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged mixed, from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle futures were called steady, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts look for live cattle to recover somewhat following another gain in boxed beef values and fairly active feedlot movement. But most most analysts look for futures weakness as cash markets are seen at or near the summer top.

Seasonally beef demand declines after retailer buying is completed for the Independence Day holiday, which should be any day, sources said. Typically, beef prices recede off after that surge, leading some market watchers to predict packers will lower bids for cash cattle next week in anticipation of declining beef prices.
Feeder cattle may find support from a higher CME feeder cattle index which rebounded up to its recent high and highest level since August 1994.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.16 at $77.76 per cwt.

But analysts also saw resistance from higher corn futures indications and poor profit margins based on current live cattle futures and fed cattle prices. Close outs or profit margins, are running in the red and demand for feeders should start to decline, they said.
